author: TEDx Talks
description:
What drives large-scale social changes like trends, fads, and collective behavior? Two powerful forces are conformity and anti-conformity: the desire to fit in and the urge to stand out. By modeling these individual-level choices and scaling them up to the population level, we can begin to understand how small decisions accumulate in surprising ways to shape the trends you follow, the customs you adopt, and even the opinions you hold.

 Kaleda is an evolutionary biologist who holds an Omidyar Postdoctoral Fellowship at the Santa Fe Institute. Her research explores how both genetic and non-genetic processes—such as epigenetics, development, and culture—shape evolution. A former Stanford Graduate Fellow, she combines theoretical and empirical research to understand significant evolutionary transitions and the emergence of cooperation, leveraging her expertise in gene-culture co-evolution and her collaborations with leaders in evolutionary biology. This talk was given at a TEDx event usi
title: How Conformity Drives Social Trends | Kaleda Denton | TEDxNewEngland

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What would you say if you were given 10 minutes to say goodbye to your child? Kate Fisher knows the answer. A rare autoimmune condition left her daughter critically ill, and the treatment keeping her alive depends entirely on blood and plasma donated by strangers. When supplies ran low, treatment was delayed — with devastating consequences.

Drawing on both lived experience and her work as a health sociologist, Kate explores a surprising contradiction: while blood donation saves millions of lives, it remains one of the least visible acts of care in modern society. Through her global advocacy initiative, Milkshakes for Marleigh, she has worked to make the impact of blood donation visible by connecting donors, recipients and communities through storytelling.

Kate examines the consequences of life-saving acts being invisible — and why understanding this may be critical to the future of blood donation. Kate Fisher is a health sociologist and global blood donation advocate whose work expl
title: The life-saving act nobody sees | Kate Fisher | TEDxBrisbane

Three questions to ask yourself when you are inventing new technology. 

Creating something new is always an exciting and intriguing process, but does a new technology or creating is going to be beneficial for the whole society, or only strengthen the inequality? What questions should we ask ourselves before taking a step forward in developing something revolutionary?  Janna is a feminist activist, a producer and a feminist writer from Kyrgyzstan, who is dedicated to promoting human rights through film and TV. She is currently doing her Master’s degree at Royal Holloway’s Producing Film and TV course. description: The talk explores a fundamental question of our time: if machines can replicate intelligence, what truly makes us human? Through real-world examples and cultural references, I intend to argue that the real question is not what AI will become—but what we might lose if we forget what makes us human. Eason Leung is a master's student in Royal Holloway, majoring in Logistics and Supply Chain Management, with an academic background in social sciences, sociology and international studies. Growing up in Hong Kong and now studying in the United Kingdom, he brings a unique cross-cultural perspective to how systems and technologies reshape human behaviour. His work explores the intersection of intelligent systems and society, with a particular focus on what it means to be human in an age increasingly defined by artificial intelligence. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

What if creativity is not just something we do, but a way of finding our path through uncertainty?

In this powerful and uplifting TEDxTruro talk, Nikita Thakrar explores how creativity can become a bridge between chaos and clarity. Drawing on the idea of dharma, our deeper purpose, Nikita invites us to see dance, expression and creative practice as tools for reconnecting with who we are, what matters to us, and how we move forward when life feels unclear.

Dance with Your Dharma is a reminder that clarity is not always found by standing still and thinking harder. Sometimes, we find it by moving, creating and trusting the rhythm within us. Nikita Thakrar is an author, educator, and founder of Journey from Karma to Dharma™. With over two decades of experience in creative arts and holistic wellbeing, she integrates movement, mindfulness, and spirituality to help people reconnect with their true purpose. description: We often celebrate connection in relationships, but rarely talk about what happens when connection breaks. In this talk, Gayathri Vamsi explores one of the most overlooked skills in parenting and human relationships: repair. Through an honest story from her own life, she reveals why mistakes, misunderstandings, and moments of disconnection are not signs of failure, but opportunities for deeper trust. This talk is a powerful reminder that strong relationships are not built on perfection, they are built on the courage to return, reconnect, and begin again. Gayathri Vamsi is an educator, entrepreneur, investor, mother, and parenting mentor whose journey spans countries, reinventions, and rebuilding life from scratch. After spending nearly a decade in Seattle working with Indian community learning spaces while raising her two boys, she moved back to Bangalore and founded Buzzing Bees, an ISO-certified education company, and co-founded Literacy Bees, an IIM Bangalore-incubated startup. author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the things we dismiss as silly, playful or completely pointless are actually some of the most important things we can do?

In this joyful and thought provoking TEDxTruro talk, Rujuta Singh explores the hidden power of silliness in a world obsessed with productivity, seriousness and constant achievement. Through humour, curiosity and human insight, she asks whether play, absurdity and purposeless acts can reconnect us with creativity, resilience, community and ourselves.

Profound Silliness is an invitation to loosen our grip, laugh a little more, and rediscover the unexpected wisdom found in doing things for no obvious reason at all. Because sometimes, the most pointless moments are the ones that remind us what it means to be fully human. Rujuta Singh is the creator of The Great Silliness Project, a year-long, community-powered exploration into the profound impact of doing utterly pointless things on purpose. Founder of Solved Together, a London-based business transformation a

Bas Breman is a researcher and teacher at Wageningen University and Research. Most of his projects are future-oriented. Renu Bohra is a seasoned Human Resources leader with nearly three decades of experience across diverse industries, including infrastructure, engineering, manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare. author: TEDx Talks
description:
We obsess over making the right choice. The right job, the right path, the right move. And the closer a big decision gets, the heavier that pressure becomes, until the fear of choosing wrong can quietly keep us from choosing at all.

But what if that fear isn't really about making the wrong decision? Sophia Guerra found an unexpected answer in a place she wasn't looking, and it changed the way she thinks about risk, direction, and what it actually means to move forward. Sophia Guerra was raised between São Paulo and Miami, an upbringing that gave her a global perspective and an early fascination with how people make decisions, and why fear so often gets in the way. A problem-solver at heart, she's drawn to the human side of design: understanding why people choose what they choose, and building experiences that help them move with more confidence.

Her work bridges behavior and technology. She studied Experience Design at Bentley University and completed MIT's Applied Agentic AI progra
title: You Can Always Hit Undo | Sophia Guerra | TEDxBentleyU

description:
The world is changing fast. Are we afraid to be ourselves?

With the rapid rise of AI, the structures we rely on are completely transforming. It’s easy to fear uncertainty and look outside of ourselves for a new blueprint or script to follow.

Sharing her journey as an introverted, first-generation Latina navigating the corporate tech world, Yvonne Armenta walks us through the moments she learned to dilute herself to fit the traditional mold of success. She shares why the answer to uncertainty isn't chasing a new strategy outside of ourselves, but doing something much braver: connecting back to who we are, and turning the parts of ourselves we were once told to dilute into our strategy a strategy that stands the test of time, no matter how fast the world changes. Yvonne Armenta is a Communications and Community Leader, Facilitator, and Storytelling & Speaking Coach. Having built her career designing communication systems for major tech and media brands, she has spent nearly a decade n
title: When the structures of success change, the strategy is you | Yvonne Armenta | TEDxBentleyU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Une chercheuse en IA raconte comment, une nuit d'insomnie, elle s'est fait piéger par la « sycophantie » d'un chatbot programmé pour flatter ses opinions. Derrière l'illusion de l'empathie, elle dévoile un piège narcissique majeur. Pour libérer notre pensée, elle nous invite à changer radicalement de méthode : ne plus chercher un confident qui nous donne raison, mais ordonner à la machine de nous prouver que l'on a tort.
An AI researcher shares how, during a sleepless night, she was caught in the trap of "sycophancy"—a chatbot engineered to constantly agree with her. Behind the illusion of empathy, she exposes a major narcissistic trap. To unlock our thinking, she challenges us to radically shift our approach: stop seeking a confidant that tells us we are right, and instead command the machine to prove us wrong. Chercheuse en IA générative, conférencière, formatrice et créatrice de contenu, Amélie Raoul étudie les enjeux liés à l’intelligence artificielle et à son éthique, un axe cent
title: Don't Ask AI for Advice. Ask It to Fight You. | Amélie Raoul | TEDxRivesdeMoselle

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Et si l'engagement n'était pas d'abord un acte de générosité envers les autres, mais une nécessité envers soi-même ?
À travers une histoire personnelle, le destin de Rosa Parks et des années d'engagement associatif, cette intervention explore une idée contre-intuitive : nous nous engageons souvent parce que nous avons besoin de sens, d'utilité et de dépassement. L'engagement implique un risque, nous expose à l'échec et nous transforme profondément. Bien avant de changer le monde, il commence par nous changer nous-mêmes.
What if commitment is not primarily an act of generosity toward others, but a necessity for ourselves?
Through a personal story, the legacy of Rosa Parks, and years of community involvement, this talk explores a counterintuitive idea: we often commit because we seek meaning, purpose, and personal growth. Commitment involves risk, exposes us to failure, and transforms us in profound ways. Long before it changes the world, it begins by changing us. Directeur général de C
title: The Hidden Reward of Commitment : Why it Changes You | Bernard Nucci | TEDxRivesdeMoselle

Peut-on s'engager sans prononcer un seul mot ? Et si l'engagement n'était pas quelque chose que nous faisons, mais quelque chose que nous devenons ?
À travers le mouvement, le souffle et la voix collective, cette intervention explore une autre compréhension de l'engagement : une compréhension qui commence par la reconnexion à soi-même. Plus qu'un appel à l'action, c'est une invitation à la présence — un chemin qui mène de la conscience intérieure à une relation authentique et porteuse de sens avec les autres.
Une expérience immersive qui montre comment l'engagement peut émerger du corps, de la respiration et du simple fait d'être pleinement vivant.

Can commitment happen without a single word? What if commitment is not something we do, but something we become?
Through movement, breath and collective voice, this talk explores a different understanding of commitment: one that begins with reconnecting to ourselves. Rather than a call to action, it is an invitation to presence — a journey

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Des opérations en Libye à la sécurisation aérienne des Jeux Olympiques, le Général Arnaud Bourguignon a passé 34 ans à décider sous haute tension. Loin des théories managériales classiques, il livre un témoignage brut sur la mécanique du commandement : responsabiliser ses hommes, apprivoiser le rapport à la mort, et assumer la responsabilité absolue des actes de ses subordonnés. Alors que le spectre d'une guerre de haute intensité plane sur l'Europe, ce talk devient un appel urgent à l'éveil d'une cohésion nationale.
From operations in Libya to securing the skies for the Olympic Games, General Arnaud Bourguignon spent 34 years making high-stakes decisions. Moving beyond standard management theories, he breaks down the raw mechanics of leadership: empowering teams, confronting the reality of loss, and fully absorbing the ultimate responsibility for his subordinates' actions. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Arrivés au camp G1-G2, on plante la tente dans la fatigue et le froid. À plus de 8000 mètres, on entre dans la zone de mort : un espace où survivre dépend d’un engagement total.
Là, s’engager ne signifie plus “vouloir” ou “décider à froid”, mais agir quand toutes les certitudes ont disparu. Brouillard, hypoxie, GPS incertain : la perception elle-même devient fragile. Et pourtant, il faut continuer à choisir, avancer, décider — car ne pas décider est déjà une décision.
We finally arrived at the G1–G2 camp and set up our tent in exhaustion and cold. Above 8,000 meters, you enter the “death zone”: a place where survival depends on total commitment. 
There, commitment no longer means “wanting” or making a calm decision, but acting when all certainty has disappeared.Fog, hypoxia, and unreliable GPS signals make perception itself fragile. And yet, you still have to choose, move forward, decide — because not deciding is already a decision. Française, Canadienne et Suisse, Entrepreneur dans l
title: À 8000 mètres, l’engagement est une contrainte de survie. | Sophie Lavaud | TEDxRivesdeMoselle

description:
Quand elle perd la vue, elle perd bien davantage que la capacité de voir : elle perd ses repères, sa confiance et une partie de sa place dans la société. Pendant vingt ans, elle lutte pour retrouver un équilibre.
Puis arrive un chien guide.
Bien plus qu'une aide au déplacement, il devient un trait d'union entre elle et les autres. Grâce à lui, les conversations renaissent, la confiance revient et l'engagement devient possible. Ce compagnon à quatre pattes transforme progressivement son rapport au monde jusqu'à lui permettre de s'investir auprès des autres et de retrouver pleinement sa place dans la vie collective.
À travers un témoignage à la fois touchant et souvent drôle, cette conférence montre comment une relation fondée sur la confiance peut devenir le point de départ d'un engagement plus vaste envers la société.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
« Une vache hors sol, c’est le début de l’homme hors sol. »
Il est facile de se mobiliser pour les icônes de la faune sauvage ou les grands fauves à l'autre bout du monde. C’est pourtant l’écrevisses des torrents, un animal de moins de 30 grammes sans physique de rêve, qui détient la clé de notre avenir. En revisitant l'héritage visionnaire de son père et les mutations de nos campagnes, l'orateur livre un vibrant plaidoyer contre notre déconnexion du vivant. Ce talk ne nous appelle pas à de lointaines croisades, mais à un sursaut de proximité : retrouver l'empathie pour la nature ordinaire, celle qui travaille gratuitement pour nous chaque jour, avant que l'avenir ne devienne définitivement sourd.

   "A disconnected cow is the beginning of a disconnected human."
It is easy to rally behind exotic wildlife icons and magnificent creatures half a world away. Yet, a tiny stream crayfish weighing less than 30 grams holds the true key to our survival. Rewinding through his father’s visionar
title: The Disconnected Human: Why Saving the Wild Begins at Home | PIERRE Singer | TEDxRivesdeMoselle

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Free time is supposed to feel relaxing, so why do so many of us feel guilty when we are not being productive? In this talk, high school student Aneesh Agarwal explores “leisurephobia,” the discomfort of doing nothing in a culture that treats busyness as success. Drawing from student life, psychology, and a famous study where people chose electric shocks over sitting alone with their thoughts, he argues that stillness is not laziness, it is a skill. Sometimes doing less is what helps us understand what we are really working toward. Aneesh Agarwal is a junior at Sunset High School who loves history as much as he loves figuring out how things work.

He’s spent the past three years building amateur rockets, is a NASA Payload Design winner, and recently wrapped up a 2.5-year project constructing a fully functional RV-12 airplane.

Outside the classroom, Aneesh is deeply involved in service, both locally and abroad. He’s built educational apps that now reach over 2,500 students in rural Ind
title: Why can free time feel uncomfortable? | Aneesh Agarwal | TEDxPortland

In this inspiring TEDx talk, Ms. Karthikaa Kannan challenges one of the most common pieces of advice given to young people: “Find your passion.” Drawing from her journey as a student, entrepreneur, content creator, and mentor, she challenges the belief that passion is something we discover by searching for it. Instead, she argues that passion reveals itself through action, exploration, and the courage to begin before feeling ready.

Through personal stories of overcoming self-doubt, challenging expectations, and building opportunities from scratch, she reveals how clarity emerges through action rather than before it. From content creation and entrepreneurship to personal growth and mentorship, her experiences demonstrate that passion is not found through waiting—it is discovered through doing.

Dylan Sapong proposes a shift in mindset to fuel your personal ambitions, passions, and happiness, ultimately leading to a fulfilled life stemming from an unexpected source. Dylan Sapong is an African-American college student attending the University of California - San Diego who challenges traditional ways of thinking and lifestyle. description: Flat-earthers aren’t “stupid”; in fact, they often hold graduate degrees, understand the importance of media literacy, and have curious minds, according to researcher and social scientist Dr. Asheley Landrum. Utilizing her background in extensive research on media biases, she asks us to question the logic behind how our backgrounds and “existing priors” shape how we view the world.  As a Faculty expert and a Senior Global Futures Sciences, and fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science, her research focuses on how identity, values, and worldviews shape the way people engage with information, especially in the context of misinformation. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Can we really trust our senses? In this talk, Batuhan Yılmaz uses illusion to show how perception shapes our reality, and how quickly that sense of certainty can break. Batuhan Yılmaz, 19 yıldır illüzyonla psikolojik unsurları harmanlayan bir sahne sanatçısıdır. İlk başarısını 2017 yılında IMF yarışmasında ödül alarak elde etmiştir. Ardından, 2023 yılında Dünya Balkan Şampiyonası’nda ülkesine çok önemli bir ödül kazandırmıştır.
Dijital platformlarda yaptığı gösteriler ve programlarla yüksek izlenme sayılarına ulaşmış, geniş kitlelere hitap etmiştir. Aynı zamanda televizyonda gerçekleştirdiği performanslarla da büyük bir izleyici kitlesine ulaşmıştır. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description: When does appreciation become appropriation? As cultural practices become repackaged as trends in mainstream media and everyday life, their histories and significance are often disrespected in the process. Pranita Kata asks you to think before you buy—to learn about the origins and traditions involved in a simple yoga class or cup of chai. Pranita Kata is a Riverside High School alumna and incoming freshman at Furman University. A cultural dance teacher, award-winning speaker, and researcher, Kata works at the intersection of service, speech, and cultural advocacy. In her talk, she shares her perspective on modern cultural expression and her experience with navigating cultural identity. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: My Culture is Not Your Costume: The Cost of Appropriation | Pranita Kata | TEDxFive Forks Youth

description: Have you ever been told to "wait until you're older?" Many of us grow up hearing that message, and for young people, that eventually becomes a reason for hesitation, doubt, and delay. In her talk, Sabrina Lin challenges the belief that impact requires perfect timing and experience. She explores how starting small and connecting with others is where real, meaningful change begins. Because if the problems we care about are happening now, why do we expect the solutions to wait? Sabrina Lin is a rising high school senior at D.W. Daniel High School. Lin is passionate about pursuing and creating educational opportunities for others. As the Co-Founder of ReadtoSucceed, she helped lead a nationwide literacy initiative that distributed more than $18,000+ worth of books to marginalized communities across the United States. Through her work, she hopes to encourage other young people to take action without waiting for the "perfect" moment. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED confere
title: The Myth of "Wait Until You're Older" | Sabrina Lin | TEDxFive Forks Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: When was the last time you were too scared to put yourself out there? Have you been scared to wear a bold outfit? To ask out your crush? Or to just speak up in a room full of people? This fear of embarrassment often feels larger than life, shaping the choices we make and the opportunities we avoid. In her talk, Stephanie Duan proposes a new outlook, challenging audiences to rethink the role embarrassment plays in their lives. Stephanie Duan is a rising senior at Riverside High School. The President of her school’s Asian American & Pacific Islander Club and an award-winning speaker, Duan uses her platforms to empower others to embrace confidence. She aims to encourage peers to express themselves authentically by modeling that same authenticity in her own life and continuing to challenge herself along the way. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Embarrassment Is Overrated | Stephanie Duan | TEDxFive Forks Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Pain is not always visible. Behind smiles and everyday interactions, people carry struggles that often go unnoticed and, thus, unaddressed. In his talk, Brian Truong challenges common misconceptions about what mental health “looks” like, redefining what strength truly means. Brian Truong is a D.W. Daniel High School alumnus and rising freshman at Clemson University. The founder of his high school’s Highlighting the Arts program and a mental health activist, Truong creates spaces where peers feel seen and supported. He aims to encourage open conversations about mental health challenges and stigmas. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Breaking Through the Surface of Mental Health Stigmas | Brian Truong | TEDxFive Forks Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world obsessed with productivity and speed, many ambitious people feel pressured to optimize every minute of their time. Slowing down is often seen as a weakness in success. However, PJ Hubbard argues that the opposite is true. This talk explores the virtue of patience as essential to living a fulfilling life. PJ Hubbard is a rising senior at Orangeburg-Wilkinson High School. An actor who has appeared in Mad Families (2017) and How to Get Away with Murder (2014), an involved student leader, and the CEO of PJcrochets, Hubbard is no stranger to stress. Through his experiences balancing numerous commitments, he has learned the secret to growth in a fast-paced world. In his talk, he shares how patience has transformed his life and how it can change yours. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Patience is Just as Precious as Time | PJ Hubbard | TEDxFive Forks Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Are you a "STEM person" or a "humanities person"? From an early age, students are often encouraged to fit into one category or the other, shaping how they view their own abilities. In her talk, Nora Numbers challenges that divide, exploring why skills in both STEM and the humanities deserve equal value and how educators, parents, and peers can better support students in discovering their full potential. Nora Numbers is a Science Hill High School alumna and incoming freshman at Brigham Young University. Numbers is no stranger to education with experience in teaching apprenticeships at local middle and elementary schoolers and as a member of her high school’s Women in STEM club. From these experiences, she has witnessed the dangers of academic labels and limiting beliefs. Numbers aims to change how education is viewed, sharing her vision for interdisciplinary academia. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. L
title: Beyond the Numbers: STEM & the Humanities Belong Together | Nora Numbers | TEDxFive Forks Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the biggest problem in conflict isn’t what people say—but what they refuse to say at all? We’re often taught to avoid disagreement and stay quiet when things get uncomfortable, but that silence can quietly make problems worse. In her talk, Bratati Chakraborty explores why people disengage in moments of conflict, from everyday situations to global issues, and why indifference can be more dangerous than disagreement. Bratati Chakraborty is a rising junior at Fountain Inn High School. As the founder of her school’s Speech and Debate Team and an advocate for equity in the field of health, Chakraborty works to encourage meaningful dialogue around critical issues. She aims to empower her peers to engage in difficult conversations rather than shy away, fighting indifference with action. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: When the World Gets Loud, Why Do We Go Quiet? | Bratati Chakraborty | TEDxFive Forks Youth

In her TEDx talk, Abby dives into how her diagnosis with hypothyroidism transformed her perspective on traditional leadership structures. By navigating the challenges of chronic illness, she discovered the power of grace and gratitude not only as a healing process but also in our lives and interactions with others. Somewhere between the myths of what healing should look like, she discovered that healing is something we all could use. 

Her work encourages others to rethink success and find a new approach rooted in compassion and connection. Abby VanVoorhis is a recent Bentley University Alumni. Abby has spent her life working on her passion for leadership. She shared in her TEDx Talk about how her diagnosis of Hypothyroidism impacted the way she views leadership and leadership structures. title: What Chronic Illness Taught Me About Coloring Outside the Lines | Abby VanVoorhis | TEDxBentleyU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Radon is a silent killer that many people in Japan have never heard of. It is invisible, odorless, and impossible to detect without proper measurement, yet it can enter homes and buildings from the ground and accumulate indoors.
In this talk, Dr. Alonso Montero explains what radon is, why it matters, and why Japan should pay closer attention to this hidden environmental health hazard. The World Health Organization (WHO) recognizes radon as an important cause of lung cancer and recommends taking action when indoor radon levels are elevated.
Using actual field experience in Japan, Dr. Montero shows how radon can be measured through long-term detectors and real-time monitors, and why action levels are important for deciding when mitigation is needed. He also shares a wake-up call from Yokosuka, where radon levels in one home reached approximately 800 Bq/m³, far above the WHO recommended action level. After mitigation, the levels were reduced, but the question remains: how many other buil
title: The Silent Killer You Haven’t Heard Of | Alonso Montero | TEDxHokkaidoU
